contract: F-11, the updates/update.log line grammar: what the app's writer r1-app emits, and what any reader must accept from every writer (plan Appendix B F-11, W-14, W-68; docs/app-updates.md 5.1 G0, 5.3 table B.2, 8.2)
frame: One append is the bytes LF, the line, LF, in one write call (G0: an empty line first, so a torn earlier append never joins it). The line: `r1-app <os> <event> <key>=<value> ... t=<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>`, bytes 0x21-0x7E only, exactly one space between tokens, at most 256 bytes without its two LFs. Never a CR, never `d="..."` (that is cmd's).

tokens.event: [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}; any other event is no line at all (skipped and counted)
tokens.key: [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}; `t` is the writer's own time key and never a caller's field; a duplicate key is dropped (the first one stays)
tokens.value: 1 to 64 bytes of [0-9A-Za-z._+-]: no `=`, `"`, `\`, `/`, `:`, space or byte outside ASCII, so no path, separator, quote or message can pass; a field whose key or value fails is dropped. This rule alone does not stop a one-word file, host or account name (`Steuer_2026.xlsx`, `DESKTOPDIT`, `peter`): the app's lines are content-free by each event's typed fields (`registered`)
tokens.time: `t=` + the UTC time to the second, the milliseconds dropped (never rounded); a time that does not match ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$ (an invalid date, a year past 9999) is omitted, as cmd lines carry none
tokens.V: a version: SemVer 2.0.0, at most 24 bytes in this log
tokens.P: an engine pin: [0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]{0,15} holding at least one digit
tokens.I: an integer: [0-9]{1,6}, read from JSON only as an integer number
tokens.E: an error code: E[A-Z0-9]{1,30} | ERR_[A-Z0-9_]{1,36} | SQLITE_[0-9]{1,5} | the literal UNKNOWN (libuv's code for an unmapped Windows error, seen on failing USB media), at most 40 bytes
tokens.C: a system call: a bare name [a-z_]+ (bareSyscall), at most 16 bytes
tokens.sentinels: `unknown` (the writer has no valid value of its own), `absent` (the source file or field is not there), `unreadable` (the source could not be read, or its value failed its rule), `none` (no stamp found; the unlock line's). None holds a digit, and every real version, pin, integer and SQLite version holds one, so a sentinel is never a value
tokens.registered: The app writes only registered events, each with a fixed field schema in a fixed order (update-log.ts, UPDATE_LOG_EVENTS): each key names one token rule (V, P, I, S, E, C) with the sentinels that key admits, or a closed list of literal values. An unregistered event is no line (skipped and counted); an unregistered key, a value failing its key's rule, or a later field of a key already taken is dropped; the fields follow the schema's order. Registered here: startup and start-failed (below); unlock is T3.10's, and P6's and P7's events join the same table as data. So the app's lines are content-free by each event's typed fields, never by the value rule alone

cap.rule: Only the app trims. After an append, when the file is larger than max_bytes and updates/applying/ does not exist, the app keeps the newest keep_bytes from the byte after the first LF in them (no LF: nothing), as bytes, never decoded, written to update.log.tmp and renamed over update.log. A trim that fails keeps the file as it is and is tried again at the next append

accept.reading: The record's reading of a line (5.1 G0 and 5.3), which every reader of update.log follows: one CR before the LF removed; spaces and TABs trimmed at both ends; an empty line is `blank`; the byte rule and the field split stop at ` d="`, after which the bytes are opaque (`time.kind` `d`); a line holding a byte outside 0x20-0x7E or TAB before that is `torn` (no reader drops it); otherwise the tokens split at runs of spaces and TABs: writer, os, event, then fields `key=value` split at the first `=`, a token without `=` or with an empty key ignored, the first of two equal keys kept, and a last field `t=` is the time (`time.kind` `t`; none: `none`). `copied` is what "Copy details for support" shows of the line: the trimmed line, every byte outside 0x20-0x7E replaced by `?`, or null for a blank line (only non-empty lines are copied)
accept.left_out: a11, a line over 1,024 bytes: whether the support copy drops it (G0) or keeps it (5.3: no reader drops an update.log line) is P6's call (CF-34), so it joins this set then

emit.how: `line` is the exact line the HEAD writer emits for the input (the time and the platform are inputs), without its two LFs; null means no line at all (skipped and counted). Every emitted line is checked against the frame and the cap too, and holds no byte outside 0x21-0x7E but its single spaces. `generic` is the frame alone, for events nobody registered (see there)

startup.sources: version: app.getVersion(). llama, whisper, kiwix: the families llama_cpp, whisper_cpp, kiwix_tools of the app's own bundled runtime-sources.yaml (absent: no such file, or no block for the family; unreadable: a read error, text that does not parse or validate, or a pin that fails P). release, release_format: the drive-release reader's answer (T3.3a, F-13): release is the record's valid app_version (absent: no file, or no valid app_version; unreadable: a read error, a damaged file, or a version over 24 bytes); release_format only when the record was read and its format is an integer that passes I, else omitted. drive_format: config/drive.json's drive_format_version (absent: no such field, or not an integer; unreadable: no file, a read error, not JSON, not an object, over 65,536 bytes, or an integer that fails I). sqlite: process.versions.sqlite. Field order fixed: version, llama, whisper, kiwix, release, release_format, drive_format, sqlite, t
startup.input: runtime_sources and drive_json: {kind: absent | unreadable} or {kind: text, text | yaml (a name in `yaml`)}; drive_release: the drive-release reader's result exactly (src/main/services/updates/drive-release.ts DriveReleaseRead); `with` replaces the named keys of `base`

start_failed.sources: version: the app version the start runner was handed (the startup line may never have been written). cause: the start failure's cause (drive_not_writable, drive_full or other; anything else other). err: the start failure's code when it passes E; else the literal UNKNOWN when that is the thrown value's code (read under try: libuv's code for an unmapped Windows error, which the gate does not show); else omitted. syscall: the thrown value's bare system call (read under try) when it passes C, else omitted. Never the message, the path or SQLite's description. Field order fixed: version, cause, err, syscall, t
start_failed.input: `thrown` is what the start threw: an Error with `message` and own `props`, or one whose `throwing_getter` property throws when read; `failure` is what the start runner hands the gate for it (src/main/services/start-failure.ts startFailureFrom, or {cause: other, code: null} when reading the value throws); `never` lists text the line must not hold

generic.sources: The frame alone (formatUpdateLogLine), the last check of every registered event's typed fields: every key and value is checked again and a field that fails is dropped; an invalid event, or a line still over 256 bytes, is no line at all. These rows run the frame on its own: the appender writes an event only once it is registered (tokens.registered; an unregistered one is skipped and counted), and they pin the frame every later registration (record 3.x, 5.4, 5.7) must fit
